name: Pilagá (pila1245, Guaicuruan)
confidence_why: 4 independent first-hand sources agree (2 agree, 1 refine), none contradicts

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim at Vidal & Klein 2002:339 n. 2 (PDF p. 19 of the author-site PDF), and both corroborating quotes (1998:195; 1997:106 n. 4) are verbatim at the stated pages; the session and are now filed under with per-page text extracts. The classification (fixed final primary stress, rule 01/001/..) matches the principal describer's flat statement made twice (1998, 2002), the later one post-dating her 2001 dissertation, and the 1997 loanword datum ([báka] > [waká]) points the same way; nothing found contradicts it. But the evidence is footnote-grade: no source we hold marks stress in data or has a stress section, the 1997 note hedged 'ultimate or penultimate' and lists never-stressed prefixes and a 'secondary shifting phonetic accent' with no rule. The best available description — Vi
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote finding re-verified directly from the PDFs' text layers (not just the saved extracts) in (1), extracted text p.19 = printed p.339 (running head 'VIDAL & KLEIN: THE CATEGORY ADJECTIVE 339'), transcription note 2, verbatim: 'Stress is not marked in the transcribed material. However, Pilagá exhibits a non-contrastive ultimate stress, and a secondary shifting phonetic accent with polysyIlabic words; Toba exhibits a non-contrastive ultimate stress.' — matches the record's deciding text (record's 'noncontrastive' = line-broken 'non-contrastive'; 'polysyIlabic' is the PDF's own scanned l/I glyph). (2) vidal_klein

sources.note: The only reference grammar of Pilagá and the only work with a phonology chapter; our final-stress coding rests on two-sentence transcription footnotes in morphosyntax articles (2002, 1998) plus a 1997 footnote that hedged 'ultimate or penultimate' and reported never-stressed subject prefixes and a 'secondary shifting' accent — the dissertation's stress section would give marked examples, settle the 1997 hedge at source, and state any rule for the secondary accent.
